songInfo.title: Shine On You Crazy Diamond (Parts I–V)

scalesUsed.notes: G - Bb - C - Db - D - F

scalesUsed.notes: G - A - Bb - C - D - E - F
scalesUsed.application: Supplies the bright major sixth interval (E natural) that gives the iconic 4-note Syd theme its haunting, bittersweet uplift

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Atmospheric, cosmic slow-blues epic contrasting dark G Aeolian minor pads with transcendent G Dorian melodic themes
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: Bb major is the relative major

mainProgression.description: Majestic minor slow-blues progression anchored by Richard Wright's synth pads and Gilmour's soaring Stratocaster solos.

sectionProgressions.progression: Bb - F - G - E over Gm

sectionProgressions.progression: Gm - Dm - Cm - Gm - Eb - D7
sectionProgressions.description: Stately 12-bar minor blues cycle with crying vocal bends and long ambient delays

harmonicFunction: Gm (i) - The dark, cavernous minor home of the entire suite
Dm (v) - Soft minor dominant maintaining atmospheric suspension
Cm (iv) - Deepens the melancholy before returning to tonic
Eb (♭VI) & D7 (V7) - Classic rock minor turnaround delivering immense classical tension before resolving to Gm

techniques.name: Singing Slow-Blues Bends & Dynamic Echo Timing
techniques.description: Holding sustained full and 1.5-step string bends with wide, unhurried finger vibrato, timed perfectly to blend with Binson Echorec tape delay repeats

notes: Four-note Syd theme: Bb (8th fret D) → F (10th fret G) → G (12th fret G) → E (9th fret G)
Slow blues solo bends on frets 15, 17, and 18 of the B and high E strings
Sustained feedback control using high amp volume and clean booster
sequence: Play the 4-note motif with authoritative pick attack and allow the Binson Echorec delay to repeat
Execute the 1.5-step bend on the 17th fret B string up to high G with support from three fingers
Apply gentle, singing vibrato only AFTER reaching the exact target pitch
Roll down guitar volume slightly to clean up the attack between phrases
tips: Gilmour played 'The Black Strat' through a 100W Hiwatt DR103 and a Colorsound Power Boost
Never rush: the space between notes creates the majesty of this piece
The E natural in the 4-note motif is the major sixth of G Dorian—it is the signature emotional pivot note

techniques.name: Syd's Four-Note Dorian Theme & Tape Echo Texture
techniques.description: Stating the haunting 4-note motif (Bb - F - G - E) with pristine attack and wide vibrato, blending with synchronized tape repeats and volume swell pads

notes: Dorian 4-note motif notes: Bb (8th fret D), F (10th fret G), G (12th fret G), E natural (9th fret G)
The major 6th (E natural) lifts the G Aeolian darkness into bittersweet G Dorian light
Set Echorec or magnetic delay to ~300ms with moderate feedback for cavernous repeats
sequence: Pick the 8th fret D string firmly with a heavy tortex pick
Shift cleanly to frets 10, 12, and 9 on the G string
Let the final E natural sing out and decay into the synth pad
Use a volume pedal or guitar volume knob for ambient swell entries
tips: Do not bend the 9th-fret E natural—hold it dead flat with gentle finger vibrato to let the Dorian color shine
Set the neck pickup for woody warmth during the ambient intro
Maintain absolute silence in the pauses to dramatize each phrase

sections.name: Part I: Ambient Synths & Gilmour Opening Lead
sections.description: Gilmour's pristine Stratocaster lead enters over the ethereal wine-glass organ drone.
notes: Play with gentle pick dynamics and allow echo to trail off
Bend the 18th fret B string up a full step to D
Apply slow, singing finger vibrato

sections.name: Part II: Syd's Four-Note Dorian Motif
sections.description: David Gilmour's immortal four-note Syd Barrett motif ringing out over Wright's Solina string pad.
notes: Let each note bloom with natural tube sustain
Accentuate the final E natural (major 6th)
Allow the delay repeats to wash across the stereo field

sections.name: Part III: Stately Minor Blues Solo (Chorus 1 - Neck Strat Warmth)
sections.description: Gilmour's masterclass in slow blues phrasing, wide vibrato, and dynamic restraint.
notes: Execute full-step bends on fret 18 of high E
Hold notes with wide, vocal finger vibrato
Use neck pickup for woody warmth

sections.name: Part III: Minor Blues Solo (Chorus 2 - Bridge Pickup Bite)
sections.description: Switching to the bridge pickup with booster engaged, Gilmour unleashes crying 1.5-step bends and emotional intensity.
notes: Reinforce bends with multiple fingers
Bite into pick attack for searing upper harmonics
Let notes sustain into gentle tube feedback

sections.name: Part IV: Vocal Verse Hook & Chromatic Line-Cliché
sections.description: The haunting vocal progression descending through a descending inner chromatic voice (G → F# → F → E).
notes: Voicing descending chromatic inner voice smoothly
Strum with relaxed, spacious dynamic breath
Support the vocal melody with understated warmth

sections.name: Part V: Saxophone & Dual Guitar Arpeggiated Coda
sections.description: Dick Parry's saxophone duel with Gilmour's arpeggiated clean rhythm guitar, leading into the gentle acoustic fade.
notes: Clean, delicate arpeggio picking across Gm and Dm
Lock tight with Nick Mason's slow, unhurried rimshot groove
Fade gently into the wind sound effects

guitar.recommended: 1969 Fender Stratocaster ('The Black Strat') with maple neck
guitar.pickup: Neck single-coil for intro solo; Bridge single-coil (Seymour Duncan SSL-1C) for biting themes

amp.recommended: Hiwatt Custom 100 DR103 through WEM 4x12 Starfinder cabinet

effects.distortion: Colorsound Power Boost (mild drive) & Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face
effects.delay: Binson Echorec 2 tape echo (or modern magnetic drum delay emulation)
effects.other: MXR Phase 90 on subtle slow setting

beginner.title: The Four-Note Motif
steps: Memorize the four notes: Bb, F, G, and E
Learn their positions on the 4th and 3rd strings (frets 8, 10, 12, 9)
Practice playing them with steady, unhurried timing

intermediate.title: Minor Blues Progression & Phrasing
steps: Master the minor blues progression (Gm → Dm → Cm → Eb → D7)
Learn Gilmour's 15th-position blues bends and release timings
Practice with a 67 BPM metronome click locking into the pocket

advanced.title: Concert Intonation & Gilmour Touch
steps: Perform the complete Part I and Part II guitar solos with exact pitch bending and vibrato
Dial in the authentic tape-echo timing and tube amplifier compression
Master volume knob dynamics and delicate pick attack nuance

commonMistakes: Rushing through the sparse phrases instead of letting the notes ring and decay
Applying vibrato too early before the string bend reaches accurate pitch
Fretting the fourth note of the motif as Eb instead of the essential Dorian E natural
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Four-note motif articulation and vibrato bloom
5 minutes: 1.5-step bending accuracy drill with guitar tuner
5 minutes: 12-bar slow blues chord rhythm comping
5 minutes: Full solo playthrough with backing track
focusAreas: Pitch precision on full and 1.5-step bends
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 67 BPM and play with relaxed, laid-back feel
Focus on landing bend peaks squarely on the beat
